domain_label: Turlock Health & Wellness — Market, Demand & Saturation Economics
purpose: A method for sizing and reading the Turlock independent health-and-wellness market: quantifying the demand base (a ~72,500 resident pool, CSU Stanislaus, the county ag/warehouse workforce and retiree musculoskeletal load, and the Assyrian/Portuguese/Punjabi/Mexican heritage communities), separating the two economic engines (insurance-reimbursed clinical vs cash/membership wellness), explaining why each sub-category saturates at the count it does across the 26 verified independents, modeling Modesto leakage and the reimbursement/wallet/supplier caps, locating defensible white-space, and expressing all revenue, margin and market-size figures strictly as labeled benchmark estimates (industry benchmark x observable size signal x Central-Valley haircut) rather than as stated facts for any named business.
assumptions: no per-business revenue, margin, payer-mix or lease dataset is supplied; every dollar figure is a labeled benchmark estimate, never an actual reported figure for any named business such as Turlock Eyecare or American Family Dentistry

the universe is the 26 verified Turlock independents in businesses.json (chains, DSOs, hospital-employed providers and corporate optical excluded), reported as a FLOOR not a census, as of the 2026-06-30 snapshot

city/county/state figures (population ~72,500, median HH income ~$82,995, license/renewal fees, the 2026 Medicare PT conversion factor ~$33.40) are cited public facts or explicitly labeled derivations

sub-category revenue bands are published industry benchmarks (revenue per provider / per practice / per studio, overhead %, COGS %) scaled by an observable size signal and a ~0.80-0.90 Central-Valley reimbursement/cost-of-living haircut, tagged estimate-not-actual with a confidence level and a confirmation path
Modesto (~218,000, ~15 minutes north, Memorial/Doctors systems plus chain/online optical) is the regional clinical anchor that caps Turlock's higher-acuity and price-shopping ceiling

the single highest-leverage confirmation for the uncertain dollar figures is primary outreach (operator interviews / vendor invoices) plus county provider-enrollment and Turlock Finance business-receipt records
two businesses (Elite Physical Therapy & Fitness, I Am Yoga Wellness Studio) straddle two sub-categories and are bi-modal, slightly inflating any strict per-sub-category tally
exclusions: per-sub-category equipment, modality, consumable and supplier-sourcing operations — covered by the supply-chain KB
per-sub-category unit-economics, cost-structure and go/no-go business-model detail — covered by the business-models KB
any claim of an actual, reported, or audited dollar revenue, margin or payer mix for a named business
chain dental DSOs, hospital-employed providers, corporate optical and national gym franchises, which are outside the independents-only catalog
individual clinical protocols, billing-code tactics, or marketing execution for a specific operator
source_description: labeled benchmark estimates and cited public facts for the Turlock independent health-and-wellness market, grounded in the health_wellness deep-dive (DEEPDIVE.md), its upstream supply_ops/market_saturation/reconciled briefs, and the 26-business source dataset (businesses.json); demand sizing uses census population/income and CSU enrollment, sub-category revenue bands use published ADA HPI / optometry GPO / APTA-WebPT / boutique-fitness and yoga operating benchmarks scaled by a Central-Valley haircut, and saturation reads use practitioner-per-capita ratios converted to per-10k
source_citation: California Demographics / Census QuickFacts 2024 (Turlock ~72,500 pop, $82,995 median HH income, median age ~34.9, Hispanic ~46%); US News / DataUSA (CSU Stanislaus ~8,455 UG / ~9,700 total Fall 2024); KQED (Assyrian ~20,000); Statistical Atlas (Portuguese ~7.3%); CDC/NCHS and FCLB/Springer (dentist and chiropractor provider ratios); Review of Optometry 2023 (solo OD income ~$212k); ADA Health Policy Institute / dental CPA surveys (dental overhead); APTA/WebPT and the 2026 Medicare conversion factor ~$33.40; DHCS via Stocktonia (2024 Medi-Cal unwinding ~17,000 county enrollees); board fee schedules (Optometry app $275 / biennial renewal $500; PT app $300 / license $150 / renewal $200); health_wellness DEEPDIVE.md, businesses.json

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEMAND_BASE names the ~72,500 resident pool with median income and age, the ~8,455-UG CSU cohort, and the ag/warehouse-plus-retiree musculoskeletal overlay, each with a cited magnitude and source confidence

competency_questions.question: Why is the sector two economic engines rather than one, and how does that split govern every downstream read?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ENGINE_SPLIT separates the insurance-reimbursed clinical engine (dental, optometry, PT, PI/auto chiropractic) from the cash/membership wellness engine (gyms, yoga, barre, maintenance chiropractic) and states the recession-resilience and binding-constraint difference

competency_questions.question: How does heritage-community trust/language fragmentation plus family-dynasty loyalty raise the sustainable provider count above the raw per-capita benchmark?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMMUNITY_FRAGMENTATION ties the Assyrian (~20,000), Portuguese (~7.3%) and Punjabi/Hispanic (~46%) pools and family-named practices (Mas Vida bilingual, Generations/Plett family) to parallel demand pools that each support an independent

competency_questions.question: How is a per-sub-category benchmark revenue band built so it is an honest estimate and never a stated fact for a named business?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REVENUE_BAND_METHOD states the benchmark x size-signal x Central-Valley-haircut method, names the public sources, and tags every band estimate-not-actual with confidence and a confirmation path

competency_questions.question: What are the labeled benchmark revenue bands per sub-category, and how is each high-gross band kept from being read as high net?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BENCHMARK_REVENUE_BANDS gives the dental, optometry, PT, chiropractic, gym and yoga bands and pairs each with its overhead/COGS reality so high gross is never mistaken for high profit

competency_questions.question: How does the provider-vs-business per-10k method work, and why should the catalog ratio sit below the practitioner benchmark even in a fully-served market?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROVIDER_DENSITY_METHOD states the count/7.25 method, the providers-counted-vs-businesses-counted caveat, and reads the gap as a leakage/consolidation signal not undersupply

competency_questions.question: Why does Turlock sustain roughly 26 independents — not 13, not 50 — and what forces set that equilibrium?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SATURATION_EQUILIBRIUM names the four demand-ceiling caps and the community floor and ties the ~26 count and the 3.6/10k aggregate to them

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FORMAT_SATURATION_READS gives per-sub-category catalog count vs realistic ceiling and a saturated / balanced / room-to-grow read for dental, optometry, chiropractic, PT, gym and yoga

competency_questions.question: How does Modesto's proximity leak higher-acuity and price-shopping demand and cap Turlock's clinical count?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MODESTO_LEAKAGE explains the ~15-minute leakage to Memorial/Doctors systems, specialist optometry/ophthalmology, large dental groups and chain optical, and ranks it the dominant external cap

competency_questions.question: How do the reimbursement, wallet and supplier caps thin the per-unit economics that would otherwise fund additional entrants?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REIMBURSEMENT_SQUEEZE names the Denti-Cal/Medi-Cal payer cap, the 2026 Medicare PT cut, the distributor concentration squeeze, and the discretionary-wallet cap, each as the binding clinical/cash constraint

competency_questions.question: Where is the defensible white-space, and which additions are crowded-out, once both demand and the entry gate are considered?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CROWDED_VS_WHITESPACE lists the crowded ceilings (optometry, independent dental, chiropractic) and the conditional white-space (referral-driven PT, a second yoga/wellness studio, niche bilingual/PI chiropractic) each only after clearing the licensing/Denti-Cal-enrollment or AB-5 gate

competency_questions.question: How is a go/no-go market verdict reached for adding a sub-category, what gate overrides a demand-true opening, and how are the reads refreshed when the figures change?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MARKET_GO_NOGO produces a verdict combining the saturation read, white-space rank and licensing/Denti-Cal/AB-5 gate (refusing demand-true but gated additions), and MARKET_REVIEW_LOOP defines the refresh cadence and material-change triggers that re-run density and saturation

glossary.definition: The defining structural fact that the sector is not one market but two: an insurance-reimbursed clinical engine (dental, optometry, PT, and the PI/auto slice of chiropractic), gated by Delta Dental / VSP / Medicare / Medi-Cal-Denti-Cal contracts, and a cash/membership wellness engine (independent gyms, yoga, barre, and the maintenance slice of chiropractic) with almost no payer billing; the clinical engine is recession-resilient, the cash engine is semi-discretionary.

glossary.term: benchmark x size-signal x Central-Valley haircut
glossary.definition: The honest revenue-estimation method used throughout: take a published national benchmark (revenue per provider / per practice / per studio, overhead %, COGS %), scale it by an observable size signal (provider count where inferable, format), then apply a ~0.80-0.90 Central-Valley reimbursement/cost-of-living haircut, yielding a band tagged estimate-not-actual with a confidence level — never a claim about a named business.

The intentional apples-to-oranges in the per-10k method: the benchmark counts providers while the catalog counts independent businesses (each may hold 1-3 providers, and chains/DSOs/hospital-employed are excluded), so the catalog ratio should sit below the practitioner benchmark even in a fully-served market; the gap is the leakage-and-consolidation signal, not proof of undersupply.

The dominant external cap: Modesto ~15 minutes north, with Memorial/Doctors hospital systems, specialist optometry/ophthalmology, large multi-provider dental groups and chain optical, pulls higher-acuity and price-shopping demand out of Turlock and is the single biggest reason the catalog ratio sits below the provider benchmark.

The binding clinical constraint: Stanislaus is a high-Medi-Cal county that lost ~17,000 enrollees in the 2024 unwinding, and Denti-Cal reimburses well below commercial PPO with heavier admin, capping how many clinical independents can subsist on the low-income majority and pushing them toward PPO/cash share — reimbursement, not input supply, compresses margin.

The counter-force that keeps the count from collapsing toward chain dominance: Assyrian, Portuguese/Azorean and Punjabi/Hispanic trust-and-language pools plus multigenerational family-practice loyalty fragment the market into parallel demand pools that each support their own independent, raising the sustainable provider count above the raw per-capita benchmark.

The discipline that every high gross revenue band is paired with its overhead/COGS caveat so high revenue is never mistaken for high profit: dental at ~55-65% overhead (70-80% sub-$750k), optometry at ~27-35% optical COGS, PT payroll at ~70% of fixed overhead, with the 2026 Medicare cut a per-visit headwind.

The reporting rule that the 26 verified independents are at least this many, never exactly all of them; the catalog excludes chains/DSOs/hospital-employed/corporate optical, rests on per-business confidence from high to medium (e.g., Turlock Smiles Dentistry, Avak's, Curl Fitness at medium), so the true independent universe could be modestly higher and is very unlikely to be lower.

The worker-classification exposure on the cash/membership engine: gyms, yoga and barre run owner-operator plus per-class-paid instructors frequently on 1099, which is exactly where AB-5 / Dynamex (ABC test) misclassification risk bites; an entrant must resolve the W-2-vs-1099 instructor question before scaling.

The two bi-modal businesses that sit in two buckets at once and distort strict counts: Elite Physical Therapy & Fitness (PT insurance-reimbursed + fitness cash, carrying both a DME/modality and a gym-capex line) and I Am Yoga Wellness Studio (yoga + Pilates/Yoga Sculpt overlapping the fitness-studio format).

nodes.definition: Catalog the demand base the 26 independents share: a ~72,500 resident pool with median household income ~$82,995 and median age ~34.9; a ~8,455-undergraduate (~9,700 total) CSU Stanislaus cohort that skews vision-and-wellness demand younger; and a large county ag-and-warehouse workforce plus a retiree base that together drive musculoskeletal (chiropractic, PT) volume above a white-collar town's baseline. These overlapping populations, not the resident count alone, set the volume that dental, optometry, PT, chiropractic, gym and yoga independents compete for.

included: ag/warehouse workforce and retiree musculoskeletal load

pros.claim: Naming overlapping demand populations explains chiropractic/PT volume a resident count alone cannot
pros.example: ag/warehouse and retiree musculoskeletal load lifts chiropractic above a white-collar town's per-capita baseline

cons.claim: Overlapping populations risk double-counting demand if treated as independent pools
cons.example: a CSU student who also lives in Turlock counted twice inflates the apparent base

failure_modes: treating CSU enrollment as net-new demand rather than partly overlapping residents
ignoring the ag/warehouse and retiree musculoskeletal overlay because it does not appear in the resident census the same way
acceptance_tests: the three demand components are each named with a public-fact magnitude (resident pop ~72,500, UG ~8,455, ag/warehouse-plus-retiree presence) and tagged with their source confidence
revisit_triggers: a census or ACS demographic refresh
a CSU enrollment release
a major local warehouse or ag employer opens, closes, or changes headcount

base.update_signal: a population, enrollment, or workforce figure is refreshed

nodes.definition: Establish the sector's defining structural fact: it is not one market but two. The insurance-reimbursed clinical engine — Dental (7), Optometry (6), Physical Therapy (3) and the PI/auto slice of Chiropractic — is gated by payer contracts (Delta Dental, VSP/EyeMed, Medicare, and heavily Medi-Cal/Denti-Cal), revolves around billing and a physical-goods supply chain, and is the most recession-resilient. The cash/membership wellness engine — independent gyms (Barre Defined, Curl Fitness, Workout Studio by KB), yoga (I Am Yoga), and the maintenance slice of chiropractic — runs on membership/class-pack/cash-pay with almost no payer billing and is semi-discretionary, the first line cut in a downturn. The binding constraint differs by engine: reimbursement for clinical, utilization plus labor-classification for cash.

included: the clinical vs cash engine split
the differing binding constraint per engine
excluded: the specific revenue bands per engine

pros.claim: Splitting the sector into two engines makes every downstream read condition on the right constraint
pros.example: reimbursement caps dental while utilization caps yoga, so a single saturation story would mislead

cons.claim: The split is imperfect because two businesses straddle both engines
cons.example: Elite PT & Fitness carries both a DME/modality and a gym-capex line, blurring the clean clinical/cash divide

failure_modes: applying a reimbursement constraint to a cash studio or a utilization constraint to a clinical practice
ignoring the dual-category straddles when assigning a business to one engine
acceptance_tests: the clinical and cash engines are each named with their member sub-categories, payer-vs-cash basis, recession-resilience, and binding constraint
revisit_triggers: a payer or reimbursement change shifts the clinical engine
a new cash/membership format opens or a straddle business changes mix
a downturn changes discretionary-wellness demand

base.update_signal: a payer rule or discretionary-demand condition changes the engine balance

nodes.definition: Explain the sector's most distinctive demand force: ethnic-community trust/language fragmentation plus family-dynasty loyalty fragment the market into parallel demand pools that each support their own independent. California's largest Assyrian community (~20,000, ~25% of the city), a Portuguese/Azorean cohort (~7.3% ancestry) and Punjabi/Sikh and Mexican (Hispanic ~46%) communities layer on multigenerational practice loyalty. The clearest visible evidence is Mas Vida Chiropractic's explicit bilingual (English/Spanish) positioning and the several family-named practices (Generations Family Optometry, Plett Family Optometry, the family-dentistry cluster). This raises the sustainable provider count above the raw per-capita benchmark.

excluded: the dollar size of each community's spend

pros.claim: Mapping community to parallel demand pools explains a count the per-capita benchmark under-predicts
pros.example: Mas Vida's bilingual positioning and the family-named optometry practices each anchor a pool a generic 73k town would not split out

cons.claim: Ancestry share is a crude proxy for clinical demand and its provider-count effect is an estimate
cons.example: a large but price-sensitive Hispanic base supports many independents but caps their per-visit revenue

failure_modes: assuming ancestry share converts linearly to provider count
treating the community-expander effect as a measured figure rather than a med-confidence estimate
acceptance_tests: at least three heritage communities are tied to anchored independents (e.g., Mas Vida bilingual, family-named optometry/dentistry) with cited population shares, and the above-benchmark effect is stated explicitly as an estimate
revisit_triggers: an ancestry/demographic data refresh
a heritage community grows or contracts via migration
a family-named or bilingual-positioned practice opens or closes

base.update_signal: a heritage-community share, migration trend, or family-practice presence changes

nodes.definition: Define the saturation-math method and its critical honesty caveat: catalog count / 7.25 (= 72,500/10,000) gives a businesses-per-10k ratio, compared against a U.S. practitioner-per-10k benchmark. The benchmark counts providers while the catalog counts independent businesses — each business may hold 1-3 providers, and chains/DSOs/hospital-employed providers are excluded — so the catalog ratio should sit below the practitioner benchmark even in a fully-served market. The gap is the leakage-and-consolidation signal, not proof of undersupply. The sector aggregate is 3.6/10k: mid-density, not collapsed and not saturated; high confidence in the arithmetic, medium in the interpretation.

excluded: the per-sub-category saturated/room verdict (its own node)

pros.claim: A transparent per-10k method with the provider-vs-business caveat prevents reading the gap as undersupply
pros.example: stating dental 0.97/10k against a ~6.0 provider benchmark shows the gap is chains/DSOs/Modesto, not a shortage

cons.claim: The providers-vs-businesses mismatch makes the gap directional, not a precise undersupply measure
cons.example: a 0.83 vs 2.4 chiropractic gap cannot be read as exact unmet demand without provider-per-business data

failure_modes: reading the catalog-below-benchmark gap as undersupply rather than consolidation/leakage
comparing the business ratio to the provider benchmark without the apples-to-oranges caveat
acceptance_tests: the count/7.25 method is stated, the providers-counted-vs-businesses-counted caveat is named, and the 3.6/10k aggregate is given with high-arithmetic/medium-interpretation confidence
revisit_triggers: a population figure changes the divisor
a national practitioner-per-capita benchmark updates
provider-per-business data becomes available

base.update_signal: a population, benchmark, or provider-per-business figure changes

nodes.definition: Establish how every sub-category revenue band is built so it is an honest estimate, never a stated fact: method = a published national/industry benchmark (ADA Health Policy Institute / dental CPA surveys; optometry GPO/COGS surveys; APTA/WebPT PT economics; boutique-fitness and yoga operating models) x an observable size signal (provider count where inferable, format) x a ~0.80-0.90 Central-Valley cost-of-living/reimbursement haircut vs national/coastal averages. Spread within each band is driven by provider count, payer/cash mix, eyewear/procedure capture, and how much demand a clinic recaptures from Modesto leakage. Confidence is the analyst's confidence in the band as a planning estimate — never a claim about any named business.

included: the benchmark x size-signal x haircut method
the spread drivers and estimate-not-actual tagging
excluded: the specific band values (its own node)

pros.claim: A transparent benchmark x size x haircut method gives a defensible band without quoting any practice
pros.example: stating a dental band as ADA-overhead benchmark x single-dentist signal x Valley haircut lets a reader audit it end to end

cons.claim: A national benchmark scaled by a coarse haircut can mis-estimate a practice with atypical payer mix
cons.example: a heavily Denti-Cal optometry/dental practice could sit well below a band built on a commercial-PPO benchmark

failure_modes: dropping the Central-Valley haircut and quoting a national/coastal band
presenting a band as a measured figure rather than a planning estimate
acceptance_tests: the benchmark x size-signal x Central-Valley-haircut method is stated with its named public sources and the estimate-not-actual tag plus a confidence level and confirmation path
revisit_triggers: a published benchmark source updates
an observable size signal (provider count, format) is measured
the Central-Valley haircut assumption is revised

base.update_signal: a benchmark source, size signal, or haircut assumption changes

nodes.definition: Build the per-sub-category revenue bands as the primary, most defensible revenue view, every one a labeled estimate, never an actual figure for a named business. Representative bands: Dental $600k-$1.0M gross/yr per single-dentist office (multi-provider scales above); Optometry $500k-$900k/yr per single-OD practice (solo OD income benchmark ~$212k); Physical Therapy ~$300k-$700k per clinic ($150k-$300k per PT, ~$75-$150/visit); Chiropractic $150k-$450k gross/yr per solo DC (auto-injury/lien higher and lumpier); Independent Gym/Fitness $120k-$500k/yr per studio (owner take ~$50k-$120k); Yoga/Wellness $100k-$350k/yr per studio (61% of US yoga studios earn <$500k/yr). Each is paired with its overhead/COGS reality so high gross is never read as high net.

pros.claim: Per-sub-category bands anchored to published benchmarks give a planning estimate without quoting any operator
pros.example: an optometry band of $500k-$900k from a solo-OD benchmark x format is auditable and business-agnostic

cons.claim: Bands rest on national benchmarks and unobserved provider counts, so any single practice can sit far outside its band
cons.example: a multi-provider dental office advertising oral surgery could exceed the $1.0M top while a Denti-Cal-heavy solo falls below the floor

failure_modes: attaching a band to a named business as if it were that business's revenue
dropping the overhead/COGS pairing so a high-gross dental or optometry band reads as high-profit
acceptance_tests: each of the six sub-categories has a low/high band derived as benchmark x size signal x haircut, tagged estimate-not-actual with a confidence, and paired with its overhead/COGS caveat (e.g., dental ~55-65% overhead, optometry ~27-35% COGS)
revisit_triggers: a published benchmark source updates
a provider count or format signal is measured for a sub-category
the 2026 Medicare PT conversion factor or Denti-Cal rates move

base.update_signal: a benchmark source or measured size signal changes

nodes.definition: Enforce the pairing that high revenue is never mistaken for high profit, the correction the band alone invites. Dental runs overhead ~55-65% of collections (70-80% for sub-$750k-collection solos: staff payroll 25-28%, lab fees 6-8%, supplies 5-6%, rent 6-7%), and Denti-Cal mix compresses margin. Optometry's exam is not the margin engine — eyewear capture is — against optical COGS ~27-35%. PT payroll is ~70% of fixed overhead with the 2026 Medicare cut a per-visit headwind. Chiropractic is dominated by owner labor + rent + liability + EHR. Gym/yoga are near-zero-COGS but payroll-and-rent heavy with utilization the lever. So a top-of-band dental or optometry gross can still net thin.

pros.claim: Pairing every gross band with its overhead reality stops a reader treating high revenue as high profit
pros.example: a $1.0M dental gross at 60-65% overhead nets far less than a smaller cash chiropractic with minimal COGS

cons.claim: Overhead ranges are national benchmarks, so the net for a specific practice is still an estimate
cons.example: without payer-mix data the exact Denti-Cal margin compression for a given office is unknown

failure_modes: quoting a gross band without its overhead caveat so it reads as profit
treating eyewear capture as automatic when it is the actual margin engine that varies by practice
acceptance_tests: each high-gross sub-category band carries its overhead/COGS caveat (dental ~55-65%, optometry ~27-35% COGS, PT payroll ~70%) and the high-gross-thin-net rule is stated explicitly
revisit_triggers: an overhead/COGS benchmark updates
a reimbursement change moves a sub-category's margin
eyewear or procedure capture economics shift

base.update_signal: an overhead, COGS, or reimbursement figure changes

nodes.definition: Rank the entry capital intensity that shapes which sub-categories can be added cheaply and which gate on capital: dental ~= optometry > PT > chiropractic ~= gym > yoga. Dental (chairs/units, digital pano/CBCT, autoclave, intraoral scanners — high six-figure build-out) and optometry (phoropter, auto-refractor, OCT/fundus camera, edger, exam lanes) are the capital-heavy, COGS-heavy formats; PT is $50k-$150k initial equipment; chiropractic adjusting tables are $1k-$5k each with optional digital X-ray $40k-$80k for PI; gym/fitness ranges $8k-$10k (small studio) to $100k+ (full floor), often leased; yoga is the lowest capex in the sector (flooring, mirrors, sound, optional heat). For the cash engine, the constraint is demand/utilization, not the cost of opening.

pros.claim: A capex ranking shows where capital, not demand, is the entry barrier and where the reverse holds
pros.example: yoga's lowest capex means its thin count is a demand ceiling, not an entry-cost barrier

cons.claim: Capex ranges are wide and equipment-leasing converts capex to opex, blurring the tier
cons.example: a leased full gym floor reads as low up-front cost despite high equipment value

failure_modes: concluding a low-capex format (yoga) is easy to add when demand, not capex, is the cap
ignoring that leasing shifts capex to opex and reorders the apparent tier
acceptance_tests: the capex tier order (dental~=optometry > PT > chiropractic~=gym > yoga) is stated with a per-sub-category equipment basis and the capex-vs-utilization constraint distinction
revisit_triggers: an equipment-cost benchmark changes
a leasing-program shift moves capex to opex
a new build-out cost datum becomes available

base.update_signal: an equipment-cost or leasing-program figure changes

nodes.definition: Explain why Turlock sustains roughly 26 independents — not 13, not 50 — as an equilibrium where four ceilings hold the count down and one floor keeps it from collapsing toward chain dominance. The ceilings: (1) Modesto leakage, the dominant external cap; (2) the payer-mix cap (high Medi-Cal, Denti-Cal below PPO); (3) the discretionary-wallet cap (median ~$82,995 holds yoga/boutique-fitness thin); (4) the supplier + reimbursement margin squeeze (distributor concentration, the 2026 Medicare PT cut, licensing barriers). The floor: community trust/language fragmentation plus family-dynasty loyalty. The result sits at a healthy-mid 3.6/10k — neither a deficit nor a glut; the genuine room to add is narrow and conditional.

included: the four ceiling caps and the community floor
excluded: the Modesto mechanism detail (its own node)

pros.claim: Framing 26 as four caps plus one floor resists both an undersupply and an oversupply conclusion
pros.example: it explains why neither a deficit nor a glut is the right read of the count

cons.claim: An equilibrium framing can imply false stability when reimbursement and enrollment are moving
cons.example: treating 26 as fixed when CSU rebound or a Medi-Cal swing could shift the sustainable count

failure_modes: reading the count as a deficit and recommending broad expansion
ignoring that the equilibrium drifts as the four caps or the floor change
acceptance_tests: all four ceiling caps and the community floor are named and each is tied to the ~26-count and 3.6/10k outcome, with the narrow-conditional-headroom verdict stated
revisit_triggers: one of the four caps shifts (Modesto draw, payer mix, wallet, supplier/reimbursement squeeze)
the community floor changes
the independent count moves away from ~26

base.update_signal: one of the four caps or the community floor shifts

nodes.definition: Give the per-sub-category saturation read by setting the catalog count against a realistic ceiling and per-10k benchmark: Dental 7 (0.97/10k vs ~6.0 provider benchmark) — most contested, chains/DSOs/hospital/Modesto absorb the rest, not undersupplied; Optometry 6 (0.83/10k vs ~1.3) — crowded for independents, near ceiling, chain/online optical competes hard; Chiropractic 6 (0.83/10k vs ~2.4) — healthy not saturated, room for 1-2 differentiated entrants; Physical Therapy 3 (0.41/10k) — under-built/white-space, Modesto hospital PT leaks demand; Independent Gym/Fitness 3 (0.41/10k) — thin, national chains own the value tier, boutiques survive on niche; Yoga/Wellness 1 (0.14/10k) — thinnest, 1-2 more could fit on the CSU + community base.

included: per-sub-category catalog count, per-10k, and benchmark
excluded: the white-space ranking and entry gate

pros.claim: A count-vs-ceiling table makes each sub-category's headroom or saturation legible at a glance
pros.example: optometry 6 at 0.83/10k reads near ceiling while PT 3 at 0.41/10k reads as white-space

cons.claim: Sub-category ceilings are themselves estimates, so a saturated/room read can flip if the ceiling is mis-set
cons.example: a chiropractic room-to-grow read reverses if auto/PI demand is lower than assumed

failure_modes: reading a primary-category count as the full picture when the two dual-category straddles shift it
treating an estimated ceiling as a hard cap rather than a directional signal
acceptance_tests: each of the six sub-categories has a catalog count, a per-10k figure, a provider benchmark where applicable, and a saturated/balanced/room-to-grow read consistent with the four caps and the floor
revisit_triggers: a sub-category opens or closes in the catalog
a demographic shift changes a sub-category's anchoring demand
Modesto leakage for a sub-category is measured

base.update_signal: a sub-category count or anchoring demand changes

nodes.definition: Model the dominant external cap: Modesto (~218,000, ~15 minutes north) with Memorial/Doctors hospital systems, specialist optometry/ophthalmology, large multi-provider dental groups and chain optical pulls the higher-acuity and price-shopping demand out of Turlock. Both upstream memos rank this the dominant external cap and the single biggest reason the catalog ratio sits below the provider benchmark. It is the specific reason a seventh independent optometry or an eighth Denti-Cal-volume dental office is not advisable. The leakage is an estimate of cross-shopping behavior, not a measured figure; a Turlock-vs-Modesto referral/cross-shop study would confirm its magnitude.

included: the higher-acuity and price-shopping leakage specifically

pros.claim: Naming Modesto leakage explains the clinical ceiling that per-capita math alone cannot
pros.example: higher-acuity dental/optometry and price-shoppers leak to Modesto's larger systems, capping a seventh independent OD

cons.claim: Leakage is inferred from proximity and scale, not measured, so its magnitude is uncertain
cons.example: without a cross-shop study the exact share of Turlock clinical demand going to Modesto is unknown

failure_modes: treating the leakage estimate as a measured figure
applying the clinical-leakage logic to cash/community formats Modesto does not actually draw
acceptance_tests: the Modesto anchor is quantified by population and travel time, tied to the higher-acuity/price-shopping clinical leakage, ranked the dominant external cap, and flagged as an estimate with its confirmation path
revisit_triggers: a Turlock-vs-Modesto cross-shop/referral leakage study is done
Modesto's clinical capacity expands or contracts
a new specialist or multi-provider group opens in either city

base.update_signal: Modesto cross-shop behavior or its clinical capacity changes

nodes.definition: Detail the three internal caps that thin the per-unit economics. The payer-mix cap: Stanislaus is a high-Medi-Cal county that lost ~17,000 enrollees in the 2024 unwinding, and Denti-Cal reimburses well below commercial PPO with heavier admin — the binding clinical constraint, reimbursement not input supply compressing margin. The discretionary-wallet cap: a median-$82,995 town with a high Medi-Cal share has a limited discretionary wallet, holding yoga/boutique-fitness thin regardless of low entry capex. The supplier + reimbursement squeeze: distributor concentration (dental big three; EssilorLuxottica/ABB in optical) and the 2026 Medicare PT conversion factor (~$33.40, net ~-1%) thin the economics that would fund additional entrants; licensing boards raise the entry threshold.

included: the supplier + reimbursement margin squeeze and licensing barrier
excluded: the Modesto external cap (its own node)

pros.claim: Separating the three internal caps shows reimbursement, not input cost, is the binding clinical constraint
pros.example: Denti-Cal below-PPO rates compress dental margin more than any consumable price

cons.claim: Some cap figures are dated facts in a moving system, so their forward trajectory is uncertain
cons.example: the 2026 Medicare PT cut and Medi-Cal enrollment are both in flux and will move the caps

failure_modes: attributing thin clinical margin to input cost when reimbursement is binding
treating the wallet cap as an entry-capex barrier rather than a demand/utilization ceiling
acceptance_tests: the payer-mix cap, the discretionary-wallet cap, and the supplier+reimbursement squeeze are each named with a cited figure (Medi-Cal unwinding ~17,000, median ~$82,995, 2026 Medicare ~$33.40) and identified as the binding constraint for its engine
revisit_triggers: a Denti-Cal/Medi-Cal rate or enrollment change
a Medicare conversion-factor update
a distributor-concentration or licensing-fee change

base.update_signal: a reimbursement, enrollment, distributor, or licensing figure changes

nodes.definition: Surface the two structural risks the demand view alone misses. Supplier concentration: the dental big three (Henry Schein, Patterson, Benco, ~85% of distributor sales) and EssilorLuxottica/ABB in optical give national distributors strong pricing power over small Turlock independents; the counterweight is buying-group membership (Vision Source/PECAA/IDOC for optical, GPOs for dental), and cash formats avoid it entirely. AB-5 classification: gyms, yoga and barre run owner-operator plus per-class-paid instructors frequently on 1099 — exactly where AB-5/Dynamex (ABC test) misclassification risk bites — so a studio entrant must resolve the W-2-vs-1099 instructor question before scaling. The supplier risk lands on the clinical engine, the AB-5 risk on the cash engine.

included: distributor concentration and the buying-group counterweight
the engine each risk lands on
excluded: supplier-specific inputs and inventory cadence (supply-chain KB)

pros.claim: Naming both structural risks shows margin and labor exposure the demand view misses
pros.example: AB-5 exposure sits on exactly the 1099-instructor gym/yoga formats the saturation read calls thinnest

cons.claim: The named supplier links are representative inference, not confirmed contracts for any practice
cons.example: a specific Turlock practice's distributor relationship is inference unless a cited source states it

failure_modes: assuming a named supplier-to-practice link is confirmed rather than representative inference
ignoring AB-5 exposure when assessing a cash-engine entrant's scalability
acceptance_tests: distributor concentration (with the buying-group counterweight) and AB-5/Dynamex instructor exposure are each stated, each tied to the engine it lands on, and the supplier-link-as-inference caveat is given
revisit_triggers: a distributor consolidation or buying-group change
an AB-5/Dynamex ruling or enforcement change
a studio shifts its instructor classification model

base.update_signal: a distributor, buying-group, or AB-5 enforcement change occurs

nodes.definition: Separate the crowded ceilings from the conditional white-space. Crowded (compete on differentiation, not count): Optometry (0.83/10k) — dense for a 73k town, the fight is product-margin defense against Costco/online eyewear, differentiation via medical eye care (Monte Vista, Avak's); Independent dental (0.97/10k) — most-contested, win on relationship/longevity (American Family Dentistry 20+ years) and cosmetic/Invisalign; Chiropractic (0.83/10k) — segmented by model (wellness-cash Atkinson/Beech, affordability Crawford, bilingual Mas Vida, auto/PI Dr. Jones). White-space, conditional on differentiation: referral-driven ortho/sports/post-surgical PT (0.41/10k, Modesto leaks demand, grow on referrals not rate); a second yoga/wellness studio (0.14/10k) recapturing demand gyms bleed off; niche bilingual or PI chiropractic.

included: the crowded sub-categories and their differentiation move
excluded: the composed per-decision go/no-go verdict (its own node)

pros.claim: Splitting crowded from white-space prevents recommending a generic seventh-of-a-kind entrant
pros.example: PT and a second yoga studio read as white-space while a seventh optometry or eighth Denti-Cal dental reads as crowded-out

cons.claim: A white-space call can read as a recommendation when each opening still needs an operator feasibility pass
cons.example: referral-driven PT ranks as white-space but depends on building physician-referral relationships first

failure_modes: recommending a generic addition to a crowded sub-category competing on Denti-Cal volume
calling white-space on demand alone without the differentiation or recapture condition
acceptance_tests: the crowded sub-categories (optometry, independent dental, chiropractic) and the conditional white-space (referral PT, second yoga/wellness, niche bilingual/PI chiropractic) are each named with their per-10k and their differentiation or recapture condition
revisit_triggers: a white-space opening is entered locally
a demographic or competitive shift changes an opening's demand
a crowded sub-category loses or gains an independent

base.update_signal: a white-space opening is entered or a crowded sub-category's count changes

nodes.definition: Define the entry gate that can override a demand-true opening, the barrier the demand view alone misses. Clinical entrants must clear California Department of Consumer Affairs healing-arts board licensure plus, to bill public payers, separate Denti-Cal/Medi-Cal provider enrollment (distinct from licensure) — Board of Optometry app $275 / biennial renewal $500; PT Board app $300 / license $150 / renewal $200; the Dental and Chiropractic boards with CE and X-ray registration. Cash-engine entrants must resolve the AB-5/Dynamex W-2-vs-1099 instructor question and carry general liability for studios. Cross-cutting: city business license, professional liability (~$1,200/mo solo clinical benchmark), ADA compliance. The market read must treat a low-capex opening as demand-true but gate-bound: the binding constraint is often the license/enrollment/classification gate, not capital.

included: the AB-5 classification gate for studios
the cited board fees and cross-cutting requirements

pros.claim: Foregrounding the entry gate prevents a demand-true opening being read as actually enterable
pros.example: a clinical opening looks open until separate Denti-Cal provider enrollment and board licensure are priced in

cons.claim: License/enrollment timelines and the AB-5 test outcome vary, so the gate is a process risk not a fixed cost
cons.example: Denti-Cal enrollment lead time and AB-5 classification outcomes differ case by case

failure_modes: recommending a clinical opening without pricing the licensure + Denti-Cal enrollment gate
treating the AB-5 classification question as optional for a studio entrant
acceptance_tests: the licensure + Denti-Cal/Medi-Cal enrollment gate and the AB-5 classification gate are each stated with their cited fees/requirements and applied as an override on the relevant white-space openings
revisit_triggers: a board fee or CE/registration requirement changes
a Denti-Cal enrollment-process change
an AB-5/Dynamex ruling shifts the classification gate

base.update_signal: a licensure, Denti-Cal enrollment, or AB-5 classification rule changes

nodes.definition: Hold the reporting discipline that the 26 verified independents are at least this many, never exactly all of them. The catalog deliberately excludes chains, DSOs, hospital-employed providers and corporate optical, and rests on per-business source confidence from high to medium (Turlock Smiles Dentistry, Avak's, Curl Fitness sit at medium). Existence and sub-category are reliable; finer operational detail (provider counts, exact payer mix, lease rates) is not independently verified. The two dual-category straddles (Elite PT & Fitness, I Am Yoga) distort strict per-sub-category counts. So '26 across six sub-categories' is the honest floor headline, the true independent universe could be modestly larger, and any saturation read built on the count inherits this floor caveat.

included: the exclusions and per-business confidence range

pros.claim: Reporting the count as a floor stops a saturation read overclaiming a precise universe
pros.example: a 0.97/10k dental read is honest only once the count is framed as at-least-26, not exactly-all

cons.claim: A floor framing limits how precisely any per-capita conclusion can be stated
cons.example: an undersupply-vs-saturated call softens when the true independent count could be modestly higher

failure_modes: treating 26 as an exact census in a per-capita conclusion
double-counting the two dual-category straddles in a strict sub-category tally
acceptance_tests: the count is stated as a floor with the exclusions named, the high-to-medium per-business confidence range given, and the two dual-category straddles flagged as count-distorting
revisit_triggers: a new independent is verified into the catalog
a per-business confidence is upgraded or downgraded
a straddle business changes its primary/secondary mix

base.update_signal: a catalog count, confidence, or straddle-mix change occurs

nodes.definition: Enforce the binding honesty discipline across every dollar figure: per-business revenue, margin, payer mix and lease are not public, so no dollar figure is ever stated as an actual reported figure for a named business such as Turlock Eyecare, American Family Dentistry or I Am Yoga. Every sub-category dollar band is a labeled benchmark estimate (published benchmark x observable size signal x Central-Valley haircut) tagged estimate-not-actual with a confidence level and a confirmation path; every high-gross band is paired with its thin-net caveat; city/county/state figures are cited public facts or labeled derivations; supplier-to-named-business links are representative inference unless a cited source states otherwise. This guardrail governs how all the sizing and band nodes may be expressed, and method + public source + confidence must travel with every number.

pros.claim: A single explicit guardrail keeps every downstream number honest and auditable
pros.example: tagging every sub-category band estimate-not-actual prevents any figure being read as an audited business revenue

cons.claim: Heavy labeling can make the analysis read as hedged and lower its perceived usefulness
cons.example: a reader wanting a single revenue number for a named practice is frustrated by a band tagged low-confidence

failure_modes: letting a sub-category band attach to a named business as that business's revenue
stating a city/county figure or a supplier link without a source or a derivation/inference label
acceptance_tests: every dollar figure in any node is a labeled estimate or a cited public fact, no named-business actual revenue/margin/payer-mix appears, each high-gross band carries its thin-net caveat, and method+source+confidence travel with every number
revisit_triggers: a new node introduces a dollar figure
a public-fact source is added or updated
an actual revenue datum (operator interview, county enrollment) becomes available to replace an estimate

base.update_signal: a new dollar figure is introduced or an actual datum becomes available

nodes.definition: Read the two dual-category straddles explicitly, since they distort strict counts and carry two cost structures at once. Elite Physical Therapy & Fitness straddles PT (insurance-reimbursed, with a DME/modality supply chain and the 2026 Medicare per-visit headwind) and fitness (cash, with a gym-equipment capex line), so it sits in both engines. I Am Yoga Wellness Studio lists Pilates and Yoga Sculpt alongside Vinyasa/Ashtanga/Hatha/Restorative/Qi Gong, adding light equipment to an otherwise prop-only base and overlapping the fitness-studio format. So '26 across six sub-categories' is the honest headline but bi-modal underneath for these two; saturation reads are unaffected, but any per-engine revenue band or count that ignores the straddle mis-assigns them.

included: the two straddle businesses and their dual engines

pros.claim: Reading the straddles explicitly prevents mis-assigning them to a single engine or double-counting
pros.example: Elite carries both a DME/modality and a gym-capex line, so a PT-only band understates it

cons.claim: The bi-modal detail adds complexity that the headline count obscures
cons.example: a clean six-sub-category tally hides that two of the 26 are economically bi-modal

failure_modes: assigning a straddle to one engine and mis-sizing its revenue or cost
double-counting a straddle in two sub-categories when tallying saturation
acceptance_tests: both straddle businesses (Elite PT & Fitness, I Am Yoga) are named with their dual engines and dual cost structures, and the count-distortion-but-saturation-unaffected note is stated
revisit_triggers: a straddle business changes its service mix
a new dual-category independent appears
a per-engine band or count is built that touches the straddles

base.update_signal: a straddle business's service mix or a new dual-category entrant changes

nodes.definition: Produce the market go/no-go verdict for adding a given sub-category, composing the saturation read, the crowded-vs-white-space call, the relevant cap (Modesto/payer/wallet/supplier), and the licensing/Denti-Cal/AB-5 entry gate into one decision. The merged rule: do not open a generic seventh chiropractic, a seventh independent optometry, or an eighth independent general-dental office competing on Denti-Cal volume — those compete on differentiation against an effectively-ceilinged count. The defensible headroom is differentiated, referral-driven PT; a second yoga/wellness studio that recaptures gym-bled demand; and niche bilingual or PI chiropractic — each viable only after clearing the licensing + Denti-Cal-enrollment (clinical) or AB-5 classification (studio) gate. A demand-true opening that fails the entry gate is a no-go until the gate clears.

pros.claim: Composing all reads into one verdict gives an actionable add/avoid call instead of scattered signals
pros.example: the verdict says no to a seventh optometry but yes to referral-driven PT once licensure and referral relationships are in place

cons.claim: A single verdict can over-simplify a sub-category whose demand and entry gate point opposite ways
cons.example: a second yoga studio has demand headroom yet still needs the AB-5 instructor question resolved before a clean yes

failure_modes: issuing a yes on demand headroom while ignoring an unmet licensing/Denti-Cal/AB-5 gate
recommending a crowded sub-category because a heritage or family anchor looks durable
acceptance_tests: the verdict for a proposed sub-category combines its saturation read, crowded/white-space call, the relevant cap, and the entry-gate status, names the do-not-add sub-categories, and refuses any demand-true but gate-bound addition
revisit_triggers: a saturation read, cap, or entry gate feeding the verdict changes
a previously gate-bound opening clears its gate

base.update_signal: a saturation, cap, or entry-gate input to the verdict changes

nodes.definition: Define the loop that keeps the market reads current. A fixed refresh cadence (re-run on each major data release) plus material-change triggers — primary outreach (operator interviews / vendor invoices) plus county provider-enrollment and Turlock Finance business-receipt records (which collapse per-business revenue, payer mix, and the true independent universe at once), a CSU enrollment swing, a major local plant/warehouse open or close, a census/ACS demographic refresh, a Denti-Cal/Medi-Cal or Medicare-conversion-factor change, or a board licensing-fee change — that send the analysis back through PROVIDER_DENSITY_METHOD and the saturation reads. Without this loop the 2026-06-30 snapshot silently goes stale as CSU enrollment rebounds, the Medicare PT cut takes effect, and Medi-Cal enrollment stays in flux.

pros.claim: A trigger list with the primary-outreach and county-enrollment confirmation keeps the lowest-confidence numbers on a path to resolution
pros.example: operator interviews plus county provider-enrollment collapse per-business revenue, payer mix, and the true universe at once

cons.claim: Too-frequent refresh churns the reads without new signal, since most inputs update only annually
cons.example: re-running density monthly when census and enrollment move yearly wastes effort

failure_modes: no cadence set so the snapshot ages silently past its reimbursement and enrollment assumptions
ignoring a fired trigger (new enrollment data) and continuing on stale estimates
acceptance_tests: a refresh cadence and an explicit material-change trigger list exist, each routing back to PROVIDER_DENSITY_METHOD and the saturation reads, with primary outreach / county enrollment named as the highest-leverage trigger
revisit_triggers: a material-change trigger fires
the cadence proves too frequent or too sparse for how the inputs actually update

base.update_signal: a material-change trigger fires or the cadence is tuned

nodes.definition: Account for the operating-cadence and seasonality the annual revenue band averages away, which are a utilization and working-capital signal not visible in a flat band. Clinical formats (dental, optometry, PT, chiropractic) run weekday daytime plus early-evening/Saturday blocks, with optometry seeing a Q4/January bump as flex-spending and vision benefits reset plus a back-to-school CSU spike. The cash engine — gyms, yoga, barre — runs the early-morning + evening dayparts with a January 'resolution' surge and a summer dip, smoothed by membership. The ag/warehouse workforce adds early-morning demand. An operator reading only the annual band will mis-plan utilization through the troughs, and the benefit-reset peaks concentrate optometry collections in a way a flat band hides.

included: clinical dayparts and the Q4/January benefit-reset bump
the cash-engine January-resolution surge and summer dip

pros.claim: Surfacing dayparts and benefit-reset seasonality turns a flat annual band into a utilization profile
pros.example: optometry's Q4/January flex-spend-and-vision-benefit reset concentrates collections invisibly in an annual average

cons.claim: Seasonality is directional without operator data, so peaks are not sized
cons.example: knowing fitness spikes in January does not say by how much without membership records

failure_modes: averaging a benefit-reset-concentrated optometry practice into a flat band and mis-planning utilization
ignoring that the cash-engine summer dip compounds with the academic-calendar trough
acceptance_tests: the clinical Q4/January benefit-reset bump, the cash-engine January-resolution surge and summer dip, and the ag/warehouse early-morning daypart are each named with their utilization/working-capital implication
revisit_triggers: a benefit-design or flex-spending-calendar change shifts the optometry peak
a membership-mix change smooths or sharpens the cash-engine swing
operator data quantifies a peak

base.update_signal: a benefit-reset, membership-mix, or daypart pattern changes

nodes.definition: Hold the honesty discipline that the upstream verdict 'the sector is structurally healthy' and that Turlock sustains more independents per capita than a generic same-size town is an editorial judgment, not a measured figure. It is well-supported on the expander (community-fragmentation) claim and on the 3.6/10k arithmetic, but the interpretation — equilibrium, healthy-mid density, narrow-conditional headroom — remains an estimate at medium confidence, never sourced data. The same applies to the saturation reads, which are estimates of competitive density not measured leakage, and to the Modesto-ceiling magnitude. This node keeps the synthesized conclusions labeled as judgments so a reader never mistakes a med-confidence editorial read for a fact.

included: the structurally-healthy verdict as a judgment
excluded: the revenue-figure honesty rule (its own guardrail node)

pros.claim: Labeling the synthesized verdict a judgment stops a med-confidence read being quoted as a measured fact
pros.example: the 'structurally healthy' conclusion is sound on the expander claim but is an estimate, not sourced data

cons.claim: Repeatedly flagging judgments can make a well-supported conclusion read as weaker than it is
cons.example: the 3.6/10k arithmetic is solid even though its interpretation is med-confidence

failure_modes: quoting 'structurally healthy' or the per-capita over-index as a measured fact
conflating the high-confidence arithmetic with the medium-confidence interpretation
acceptance_tests: the structurally-healthy verdict and the per-capita over-index are stated as medium-confidence judgments, distinct from the high-confidence 3.6/10k arithmetic, with the saturation-reads-are-estimates rule named
revisit_triggers: a primary-data source upgrades a judgment to a measured figure
a saturation read is challenged by new leakage data
the equilibrium interpretation is revised

base.update_signal: a synthesized judgment is upgraded by primary data or revised

edges.why_related: the clinical-vs-cash engine split is read against the demand base and its overlays
heritage anchoring refines the broad demand base into community-specific demand pools
the per-10k density divisor is the resident base named among the demand drivers
the band method conditions on which engine (payer vs cash) a sub-category belongs to

the per-sub-category bands are the values produced by applying the band-construction method
which sub-categories and anchored independents exist to band comes from the heritage map
the overhead/COGS pairing corrects the gross bands into a net-aware read
the capex ranking distinguishes the capital-heavy clinical engine from the lower-capex cash engine
the equilibrium read aggregates the per-10k density into the 3.6/10k whole
the community floor that keeps the count from collapsing comes from the fragmentation map
the equilibrium applies the right cap (reimbursement vs wallet) per engine
per-sub-category reads decompose the overall equilibrium into count-vs-ceiling calls
the dominant external cap in the equilibrium is detailed in the leakage node
the payer/wallet/supplier caps in the equilibrium are detailed in the squeeze node
the squeeze names the binding constraint for each engine the split establishes
the supplier risk lands on the clinical engine and the AB-5 risk on the cash engine the split defines
distributor concentration is the supplier face of the same margin-squeeze force
the crowded and white-space calls are the saturated and under-built ends of the per-sub-category reads
the white-space PT call depends on the Modesto leakage that under-builds local PT
the crowded-dental call rests on the Denti-Cal reimbursement cap that commoditizes volume
the entry gate is applied as an override on each white-space opening
demand ranks an opening attractive while the licensing/Denti-Cal/AB-5 gate can make it un-enterable, pulling opposite ways
edges.resolution_rule: a demand-true opening is a no-go until its entry gate (board licensure + Denti-Cal/Medi-Cal enrollment for clinical, AB-5 classification for studios) is cleared; demand never overrides an unmet gate

edges.why_related: the AB-5 classification exposure is the studio face of the entry gate
the floor caveat qualifies the per-sub-category counts the saturation reads are built on
the guardrail governs how the per-sub-category bands may be expressed and labeled
the high-gross/thin-net pairing is the margin face of the honesty discipline the guardrail enforces
the straddle read identifies the two businesses that sit in both engines the split defines
the bi-modal straddle read builds on the per-sub-category bands to size the two dual-engine businesses
the verdict elevates the highest white-space openings and rejects the crowded additions
the verdict applies the entry gate as the override that can turn a demand-true yes into a no
the verdict weighs the dominant Modesto cap when rejecting a crowded clinical addition
the verdict must express any revenue rationale as a labeled estimate under the guardrail
the review loop watches the inputs to the verdict and re-triggers it when they change
the daypart and benefit-reset seasonality is read per engine the split defines

conflict_axes.name: demand_headroom_vs_entry_gate
conflict_axes.description: A sub-category can be demand-true white space yet be walled off by board licensure, Denti-Cal enrollment, or AB-5 classification, so the demand and feasibility views point opposite ways.
poles: block on the unmet entry gate
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat a demand-true opening as a no-go until its entry gate clears; demand never overrides licensure/enrollment/classification

conflict_axes.name: high_gross_vs_thin_net
conflict_axes.description: A top-of-band gross (dental, optometry) and its overhead/COGS reality cannot both characterize profitability; high revenue is not high net.
poles: read the high-gross band as success
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: always pair the gross band with its overhead/COGS caveat before any profitability read

conflict_axes.name: provider_benchmark_vs_business_count
conflict_axes.description: The practitioner-per-10k benchmark counts providers while the catalog counts businesses, so a catalog-below-benchmark gap is consolidation/leakage, not undersupply.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: expect the business ratio below the provider benchmark even when fully served; read the gap directionally, not as unmet demand

conflict_axes.name: community_floor_vs_modesto_ceiling
conflict_axes.description: Heritage/family-loyalty fragmentation pushes the provider count above population prediction while Modesto's gravity pulls higher-acuity demand away and caps it.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the community floor raises the count for trust/language-anchored independents; Modesto caps higher-acuity clinical; apply each to the formats it governs

conflict_axes.name: reimbursement_cap_vs_input_cost
conflict_axes.description: Thin clinical margin can be blamed on input/supply cost when reimbursement (Denti-Cal below PPO, the 2026 Medicare PT cut) is the actual binding constraint.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: for the clinical engine, reimbursement is the binding constraint; input cost is secondary except where distributor concentration bites

conflict_axes.name: utilization_cap_vs_entry_capex
conflict_axes.description: A low-capex cash format (yoga) can look easy to add on capital when demand/utilization, not entry cost, is the binding cap.
poles: block because utilization demand is capped
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: for the cash engine, read utilization/discretionary-wallet demand as the cap, not entry capex; low capex does not mean open headroom

conflict_axes.name: estimate_labeling_vs_decisiveness
conflict_axes.description: Rigorous estimate-not-actual labeling protects honesty but can make the analysis read as too hedged to act on.
poles: label every figure as an estimate
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: label every figure but pair it with a confidence and a confirmation path so the read stays actionable without overclaiming a named-business figure

conflict_axes.name: coverage_floor_vs_precise_census
conflict_axes.description: The 26 are a verified floor, not a census, so a per-capita saturation verdict cannot be stated as precisely as an exact-count read invites.
poles: treat the count as an exact census
treat the count as an at-least floor
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: read 26 as at-least-26 with exclusions named; soften any per-capita conclusion to reflect the floor and the two straddles

conflict_axes.name: snapshot_stability_vs_trend_drift
conflict_axes.description: The ~26 equilibrium reads as stable, but rebounding CSU enrollment, the new Medicare PT cut, and Medi-Cal flux are moving the underlying forces.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold the 2026-06-30 snapshot as a dated baseline but let the review loop, not assumption, decide when drift has moved the equilibrium

edge_cases.description: A sub-category band is attached to a named business as if it were that business's actual revenue
edge_cases.trigger: a per-sub-category estimate is quoted next to a specific practice's name (e.g., Turlock Eyecare)
edge_cases.mitigation: keep every band sub-category-level and estimate-not-actual; never bind a dollar figure to a named business as fact

edge_cases.description: A high-gross dental or optometry band is read as high profit
edge_cases.trigger: a top-of-band gross is quoted without its overhead/COGS caveat
edge_cases.mitigation: pair every gross band with its overhead (~55-65% dental) or COGS (~27-35% optometry) reality before any profitability read

edge_cases.description: The catalog-below-benchmark per-10k gap is read as undersupply
edge_cases.trigger: the business ratio is compared to the provider benchmark without the apples-to-oranges caveat
edge_cases.mitigation: expect the business ratio below the provider benchmark even when fully served; read the gap as consolidation/leakage

edge_cases.description: A demand-true clinical opening is recommended without pricing the licensure + Denti-Cal enrollment gate
edge_cases.trigger: a PT or dental opening is judged on demand headroom alone
edge_cases.mitigation: apply board licensure + separate Denti-Cal/Medi-Cal provider enrollment as an override before any clinical yes

edge_cases.description: A low-capex yoga/studio opening ignores the AB-5 instructor-classification gate
edge_cases.trigger: a studio concept is treated as cheap, easy entry on capital alone
edge_cases.mitigation: require the W-2-vs-1099 AB-5/Dynamex instructor question be resolved before scaling a studio entrant

edge_cases.description: Chiropractic is read as saturated because there are six clinics
edge_cases.trigger: the count is compared to a small-town intuition without the per-10k and model-segmentation view
edge_cases.mitigation: read chiropractic at 0.83/10k vs a ~2.4 provider benchmark, segmented by model (cash/affordability/bilingual/PI) — healthy with room for 1-2 differentiated

edge_cases.description: Thin clinical margin is blamed on consumable input cost
edge_cases.trigger: a margin-squeeze read attributes it to supplies rather than reimbursement
edge_cases.mitigation: identify Denti-Cal-below-PPO and the 2026 Medicare cut as binding; input cost is secondary except where distributor concentration bites

edge_cases.description: A dual-category straddle is double-counted or mis-assigned to one engine
edge_cases.trigger: Elite PT & Fitness or I Am Yoga is tallied in two sub-categories or sized on one engine's band
edge_cases.mitigation: use primary category as the spine, note the bi-modal second engine, and size with both cost structures without double-counting

edge_cases.description: The 26-count is treated as an exact census in a per-capita conclusion
edge_cases.trigger: a saturation verdict leans on 26 as the complete independent universe
edge_cases.mitigation: read 26 as an at-least floor with chains/DSOs/hospital/optical excluded; soften the per-capita conclusion accordingly

edge_cases.description: A supplier-to-named-practice link is asserted as a confirmed contract
edge_cases.trigger: a named distributor is stated to serve a specific Turlock practice without a cited source
edge_cases.mitigation: treat the supplier universe as verified-to-geography but the specific practice link as representative inference unless cited

edge_cases.description: Primary outreach or county enrollment data arrives and contradicts the estimated bands and universe
edge_cases.trigger: operator interviews / vendor invoices / county provider-enrollment become available
edge_cases.mitigation: fire the review loop, replace the estimated revenue/payer-mix/universe figures with the measured data, and re-derive the bands and saturation reads

workflow.description: Record the resident pool, CSU enrollment, and the ag/warehouse-plus-retiree musculoskeletal overlay with cited magnitudes
workflow.gate: the three demand components each have a public-fact magnitude and a source confidence

workflow.description: Assign each sub-category to the insurance-reimbursed clinical or cash/membership wellness engine with its binding constraint
workflow.gate: both engines are named with members, payer-vs-cash basis, recession-resilience, and binding constraint

workflow.description: Tie the Assyrian/Portuguese/Punjabi/Hispanic pools and family-named practices to parallel demand pools
workflow.gate: at least three communities are tied to anchored independents with cited shares and the above-benchmark effect stated

workflow.description: Compute count/7.25 per-10k against the practitioner benchmark with the providers-vs-businesses caveat
workflow.gate: the method, the apples-to-oranges caveat, and the 3.6/10k aggregate are stated with confidence

workflow.action: Build the labeled benchmark revenue bands
workflow.description: Derive each sub-category band as benchmark x size signal x Valley haircut, paired with its overhead/COGS caveat
workflow.gate: every band is estimate-not-actual with a size signal, confidence, and overhead/COGS pairing

workflow.description: Tie the ~26 count and 3.6/10k to the four ceiling caps and the community floor
workflow.gate: all four caps and the floor are named and tied to the ~26-count and narrow-conditional headroom

workflow.description: Set each sub-category's catalog count against its per-10k ceiling and a saturated/balanced/room read
workflow.gate: each sub-category has a count, per-10k, benchmark, and saturation read consistent with the caps and floor

workflow.action: Model Modesto leakage and the internal caps
workflow.description: Quantify the Modesto anchor and name the payer/wallet/supplier caps as the binding constraints
workflow.gate: Modesto is quantified and ranked dominant; the payer/wallet/supplier caps are each named with a cited figure

workflow.description: Name the crowded ceilings and the conditional white-space openings with their differentiation/recapture condition
workflow.gate: crowded and white-space sub-categories are each named with their per-10k and condition

workflow.description: Mark each white-space opening viable only after its licensure/enrollment or AB-5 gate clears
workflow.gate: the clinical and studio entry gates are stated with cited fees/requirements and applied as overrides

workflow.action: Compose the go/no-go verdict and review loop
workflow.description: Combine saturation, white-space, caps, and entry gate into an add/avoid call and set the refresh triggers
workflow.gate: the verdict refuses any demand-true but gate-bound addition and names the do-not-add sub-categories

dominance_rules.rule: The revenue-honesty guardrail dominates any pressure for a single decisive named-business number
dominance_rules.rationale: no per-business revenue/margin/payer-mix is public, so an over-decisive figure would be a fabrication
dominance_rules.trigger: a request for a named practice's revenue or a single market number
dominance_rules.action: answer only with a labeled estimate (benchmark x size signal x Valley haircut) plus confidence and confirmation path

dominance_rules.rule: The entry gate dominates a demand-true white-space opening
dominance_rules.rationale: board licensure, Denti-Cal enrollment, or AB-5 classification can make a high-demand opening un-enterable
dominance_rules.trigger: a white-space opening is judged attractive on demand alone
dominance_rules.action: mark it a no-go until the clinical licensure+enrollment or studio AB-5 gate clears

dominance_rules.rule: The overhead/COGS net read dominates the high-gross band
dominance_rules.rationale: a top-of-band dental or optometry gross can still net thin
dominance_rules.trigger: a high-gross band is used to characterize profitability
dominance_rules.action: pair it with its overhead/COGS caveat before any profit read

dominance_rules.rule: The reimbursement constraint dominates input cost for the clinical engine
dominance_rules.rationale: Denti-Cal-below-PPO and the 2026 Medicare cut compress margin more than consumable price
dominance_rules.trigger: thin clinical margin is attributed to input cost
dominance_rules.action: identify reimbursement as binding; treat input cost as secondary except where distributor concentration bites

dominance_rules.rule: The Modesto ceiling dominates per-capita demand math for higher-acuity clinical formats
dominance_rules.rationale: cross-shopping leaks higher-acuity and price-shopping demand to the larger neighbor regardless of local math
dominance_rules.trigger: a seventh optometry or eighth Denti-Cal dental is justified on Turlock demand alone
dominance_rules.action: cap the higher-acuity clinical format and decline the addition

dominance_rules.rule: Utilization/wallet demand dominates entry capex for the cash engine
dominance_rules.rationale: a low-capex studio is still capped by discretionary-wallet utilization, not entry cost
dominance_rules.trigger: a yoga/fitness opening is called easy because capex is low
dominance_rules.action: read the utilization/wallet cap as binding, not the low capex

dominance_rules.rule: The providers-vs-businesses caveat dominates a raw per-10k undersupply read
dominance_rules.rationale: the benchmark counts providers while the catalog counts businesses, so the gap is expected even when served
dominance_rules.trigger: a catalog-below-benchmark gap is read as undersupply
dominance_rules.action: read the gap as consolidation/leakage and require provider-per-business data before any undersupply call

dominance_rules.rule: The coverage-floor rule dominates an exact-census per-capita conclusion
dominance_rules.rationale: the 26 are a verified floor with chains/DSOs/hospital/optical excluded
dominance_rules.trigger: a saturation verdict leans on 26 as the complete universe
dominance_rules.action: read 26 as at-least-26 and soften the per-capita conclusion accordingly

dominance_rules.rule: A flagged low-confidence input dominates a confident downstream conclusion built on it
dominance_rules.rationale: a conclusion cannot be more certain than its weakest load-bearing input
dominance_rules.trigger: a revenue band or capture/leakage estimate carries a conclusion above its own confidence
dominance_rules.action: cap the conclusion's confidence at that of its weakest input and name the confirmation source

anti_rework_rules.rule: Split the two engines before sizing bands or reading saturation
anti_rework_rules.prevents: applying a reimbursement cap to a cash studio or a utilization cap to a clinical practice, forcing a re-read

anti_rework_rules.rule: Label every dollar figure estimate-not-actual at the moment it is written
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a later honesty sweep that must re-caveat figures already quoted as named-business facts

anti_rework_rules.rule: Pair every high-gross band with its overhead/COGS caveat when the band is built
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a profitability read on a gross band that must be reworked once the thin-net reality is surfaced

anti_rework_rules.rule: State the providers-vs-businesses caveat the first time a per-10k figure is used
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an undersupply conclusion drawn from a gap that must be retracted once the caveat is applied

anti_rework_rules.rule: Apply the entry gate while ranking white-space, not after recommending it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: recommending a clinical or studio opening that the licensure/Denti-Cal/AB-5 gate then voids

anti_rework_rules.rule: Report the count as a floor and note the two straddles before any saturation tally
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an exact-census per-capita conclusion and double-counted straddles that must be re-tallied

anti_rework_rules.rule: Identify reimbursement as the binding clinical constraint before attributing margin to inputs
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a supply-cost margin story that must be redone once reimbursement is recognized as binding

anti_rework_rules.rule: Name the primary-outreach / county-enrollment confirmation path on every low-confidence dollar figure as it is stated
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a later pass to attach confirmation sources to numbers already published without them

anti_rework_rules.rule: Label the structurally-healthy verdict and the per-capita over-index as judgments the first time they are stated
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a med-confidence editorial read being quoted downstream as a measured fact and then having to be re-caveated

iteration_protocol.trigger: primary outreach (operator interviews / vendor invoices) plus county provider-enrollment or Turlock Finance business-receipt records become available
iteration_protocol.action: replace the per-business revenue, payer-mix, and true-universe estimates with measured figures and re-derive the bands and saturation reads

iteration_protocol.trigger: a census/ACS demographic or CSU enrollment refresh lands
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the demand base and heritage/community demand and re-run the per-10k density

iteration_protocol.trigger: a Denti-Cal/Medi-Cal rate or enrollment change, or a Medicare conversion-factor update
iteration_protocol.action: re-read the reimbursement squeeze and re-pair the affected clinical revenue bands

iteration_protocol.trigger: a major local plant, warehouse, or distribution center opens or closes
iteration_protocol.action: update the ag/warehouse demand component and re-read the affected saturation and white-space

iteration_protocol.trigger: a sub-category opens or closes in the catalog
iteration_protocol.action: re-tally the saturation reads and refresh the floor caveat

iteration_protocol.trigger: a board licensing/CE fee or Denti-Cal enrollment process changes, or an AB-5/Dynamex ruling shifts
iteration_protocol.action: re-price the entry gate and re-issue any affected go/no-go verdicts

iteration_protocol.trigger: a distributor consolidation or buying-group change moves small-operator input pricing
iteration_protocol.action: re-read the supplier risk and re-pair the affected revenue bands with refreshed cost reality

iteration_protocol.trigger: a Modesto clinical-capacity change (a new specialist or multi-provider group) shifts cross-shopping
iteration_protocol.action: re-estimate Modesto leakage and re-read the higher-acuity saturation

priority_rationale: The demand base, the two-engine split, and community fragmentation are foundational because density, sizing, saturation, and white-space all read from them; the provider-vs-business density method and the band-construction method precede the per-sub-category bands and the high-gross/thin-net correction they constrain; the saturation equilibrium, per-sub-category reads, Modesto leakage, and the reimbursement/wallet/supplier caps build on the demand and band layers; crowded-vs-white-space and the entry gate compose the competitive view; the revenue-honesty guardrail and the coverage-floor caveat govern every dollar and count expression; and the go/no-go verdict plus the review loop come last because they compose all upstream reads into a decision and a self-correcting refresh.
